method: Direct reading by the running Terra agent of files under C:\CharityGraph-runtime\reality-megarun-8-rich-semantic-furnace\representations; no generated claim templates.

items.claim: Australian Red Cross reports that its disaster preparedness, relief and recovery work is based on five named psychosocial principles: safety, calm, connection, self-efficacy and hope.
items.scope: organisation disaster work described on this report page
items.why: The named five-principle list is inseparable from the program claim.

items.claim: The report says Emergency Services activated in response to 70 events between July 2023 and 24 June 2024.
items.why: Count, operational unit and interval must travel together.

items.claim: World Vision Australia says it undertakes scheduled evaluations and reviews of programs and projects to assess impact on participants’ lives, with attention to vulnerable or excluded people including people with disability, women and children.
items.why: This is a declared practice, not a finding of impact.

items.claim: The report says it conducted 12 evaluations and reviews in 2024: seven evaluations and five mid-term reviews.
items.why: The total and components should be modelled as one observation.

items.claim: The Smith Family reports 5,478 individual volunteers filling 5,983 volunteer roles nationally, noting that some volunteers held more than one role.
items.why: Persons, roles and the many-to-one caveat cannot be honestly flattened.

items.claim: The page includes a named Learning Club volunteer’s account of tutoring; it is testimonial evidence, not evidence that all students or volunteers experience the stated benefits.
items.why: A product must visibly distinguish anecdote from aggregate outcome evidence.

items.claim: ACFID describes AP4D as a tripartite initiative hosted by ACFID and funded by ACMC and DFAT, bringing together policy experts across Australia and the region.
items.why: Host and funder roles have direction and cannot be one undifferentiated partner edge.

items.claim: ACFID reports that AP4D made submissions to some policy processes while other policy documents reflected its themes without AP4D having submitted to them.
items.why: This defeats a naive claim that thematic similarity proves causal policy influence.

items.claim: WWF-Australia states that it is an ACFID Code signatory and says it is committed to and fully adheres to the Code.
items.why: Do not turn self-asserted adherence into independent verification.

items.claim: The page says the ACFID Code offers a public complaint mechanism; it does not report any complaint outcome or establish actual conduct compliance.
items.why: Availability of a mechanism is not outcome evidence.
